narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>The number is nineteen, because I add two, three, three and eleven together.
<bookmark mark='test'/>But nineteen is a prime number itself, so none of those primes divide it exactly.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>The primes of a number are multiplied to make it, never added.
removed_beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble says the number is nineteen, from adding 2, 3, 3 and 11; a small check shows 19 has no factor 2, 3 or 11; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>To check, divide the number by each prime in turn, and you must end at the last prime.
<bookmark mark='back'/>One hundred and ninety eight divided by two is ninety nine. Then you reach thirty three, then eleven, which is prime.
removed_beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the anchor; the recap board shows the check: 198 ÷ 2 = 99, 99 ÷ 3 = 33, 33 ÷ 3 = 11

old_misconception.wrong_move: Chintu says the number is nineteen, because he adds two, three, three and eleven. A prime factorisation multiplies the primes, so nineteen is not the number and the bubble is struck.
